learningObjectives: Understand how the final amount is calculated with A=P*(1+r/(100*n))^(n*t) using the starting amount, annual rate, compounding frequency and time
Explain how changing the annual rate and time changes the final amount, similar to how different time scales affect change in physical systems
Apply the formula to predict amounts with yearly, quarterly and monthly compounding

explanations.text: A starting amount grows when interest is added repeatedly using A=P*(1+r/(100*n))^(n*t). P is the initial value before any growth is applied, similar to how new material builds up from a starting process over time.

evidence.quote: Plutonium is created in a reactor when uranium atoms absorb neutrons.

scenario.settingLabel: Interest compounded yearly for science fund
